items.title: Delete the duplicate bare-string validate.commands entry and keep the focus-tagged object
items.context: lattice.config.json validate.commands index 4 (bare string) duplicates index 12 (object with focus:[fast]). commandFromString in packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts parses the bare string into an identical command/args pair with no shell, so the two entries share one execution identity apart from the focus selection tag. Keep index 12: unfocused runs execute every configured command, and only focus-tagged commands survive validate --focus=fast.

happy.desc: After the edit, lattice.config.json parses and validate.commands contains exactly one entry whose command line references reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js, and it is the object carrying focus:[fast].

edge.desc: The surviving entry keeps the identical execution identity: command node, the same single script arg, and no shell, cwd, env, timeoutMs or optional field, so no argument, timeout, execution context or fail-closed behaviour changes.
Every other validate.commands entry is byte-identical before and after the edit, and the list length drops by exactly one.

adversarial.desc: The removal does not drop the smoke from the fast focus set: filtering validate.commands by focus fast still selects reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js after the edit.

verificationEvidence.note: git show 304d459c8d reports 1 file changed, 1 deletion(-) and the diff contains exactly one removed line, the bare string entry. An ordered-subsequence comparison of the pre-edit (48) and post-edit (47) normalised lists consumed all 47 post entries with that single removal, so no other entry was added, removed, reordered or reworded.

Post-edit scan: validate.commands length 47 and exactly one entry references reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js, namely {command:node, args:[packages/main/dist/tasks/reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js], focus:[fast]}. grep -c on the file also prints 1 and the file parses as JSON.

verificationEvidence.command: node -e "filter validate.commands by focus includes fast"
verificationEvidence.note: Filtering post-edit validate.commands for entries whose focus array includes fast still yields the reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js entry, so the removal did not drop the smoke from the fast focus set that filterFocusedConfiguredCommands (verifier.ts:184) selects.

verificationEvidence.command: node -e "print the surviving entry and its keys"
verificationEvidence.note: The surviving entry declares only command, args and focus: no shell, cwd, env, timeoutMs or optional field, exactly as both pre-edit entries did, so execution identity is unchanged and arguments, timeout, execution context and fail-closed behaviour are preserved. The runner confirms it: the validate progress record spawned it as node packages/main/dist/tasks/reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js timeoutMs=270000, the same default timeout other untimed entries receive, and it exited code=0 in 2488ms.

items.title: Prove from validate invocation records that the smoke runs exactly once and rescan for other duplicates
items.context: Verify against the runner's own invocation record (validate --json command results), not just a zero exit code. Also rescan validate.commands for any other pair with identical full execution identity, and confirm that same-script pairs differing in meaningful execution parameters are left untouched.
items.userSees: The validate --json command records contain exactly one entry for reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js and the duplicate scan reports no remaining full-identity duplicates

happy.desc: A real lattice validate run reports exactly one command result for reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js in its invocation record, and that result passes.

edge.desc: A full-identity duplicate scan over all validate.commands entries reports zero remaining duplicate groups.

adversarial.desc: The same-script scan is reported separately from the full-identity scan, so any pair sharing a script path but differing in meaningful execution parameters is surfaced and deliberately preserved rather than removed.

verificationEvidence.note: Invocation record from a real unfocused validate run in this worktree. The runner announced "running 47 configured validate.command(s)" (was 48) and its per-command record contains exactly one invocation of the smoke: "command 12/47 started configured validate.commands[11]: node packages/main/dist/tasks/reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.js timeoutMs=270000" followed by "command 12/47 ended configured validate.commands[11]: code=0 elapsedMs=2488". Exactly one start line and one end line reference that script, and it passed. NOTE: the surrounding run did not finish - an unrelated command (delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js) hit its 270s timeout and the run then hit the global 900s cap, under a host load average of ~371 caused by other concurrent sessions. That abort is unrelated to this change and does not affect the exactly-once count, which is established by the per-command record above.

Post-edit full-identity scan (serialising every field: command, args, shell, cwd, env, timeoutMs, optional, focus) over all 47 entries reports zero duplicate groups. A second scan keyed on execution identity alone (ignoring the focus and label selection tags) also reports zero duplicates.

verificationEvidence.command: node -e "same-script-path scan over validate.commands, reported separately"
verificationEvidence.note: The same-script scan is run and reported separately from the full-identity scan. Pre-edit it found exactly one same-script pair (indexes 4 and 12, the duplicate), and no other entry in the list shares a script path with different execution parameters, so nothing differentiated existed that could have been removed by mistake. Post-edit the same-script scan reports zero remaining pairs, confirming only the true duplicate was removed.
